- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price (e.g., 70→80 range); cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 80→70→65), model often holds too high; apply downward bias in next 3–5 days if sentiment is weak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ trend if sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; force a 1–3% downward correction if true price drops >2% from peak.
